title: Design Studio Selections Training Note: Design Credit Offset in Option Deposits
content:
**Q. How does design credit on a Design Studio Selections file reduce the finish group of the option deposit?**
Through the credit offset, which is set by the design credit standing on the file:

- where builder goodwill credit granted on the file is not yet fully applied, the credit offset is all design credit granted on the file less any credit forfeited;
- where only credit of other sources stands unapplied, the credit offset is the credit already applied plus 0.5 (one half) of the unapplied credit;
- where no credit stands unapplied, the credit offset is the credit already applied.

**Q. What is "unapplied" credit?**
The design credit granted on the file less the credit forfeited and less the credit already applied to option lines, never below zero. Builder goodwill credit is not fully applied while the builder goodwill credit granted exceeds the builder goodwill credit applied.

**Q. Which records are read?**
The credit grants, credit applications and credit forfeitures on the design ledger, with the credit source of each (package allowance, promotional credit, builder goodwill).

**Q. Worked figures?** Hypothetical file: credit granted 3000.00 (2700.00 package allowance, 300.00 builder goodwill), nothing forfeited, 1800.00 applied, all of it package allowance.

| Standing | Offset |
|---|---|
| As above: builder goodwill 300.00 not applied | 3000.00 |
| Had the 300.00 builder goodwill been fully applied, leaving 900.00 of package allowance unapplied | 2100.00 plus 0.5 of 900.00, that is 2550.00 |
| Had every credit been applied | 3000.00 applied: 3000.00 |
